t: Tawantinsuyu, the largest pre-Columbian state of the Americas, stretched some 4,000 km from southern Colombia to central Chile.
It ran on labour tribute, storehouses, a 40,000 km road network and khipu records, without money or alphabetic writing.
Smallpox and a civil war between Huáscar and Atahualpa left it open to Francisco Pizarro’s conquest in 1532–1533.
dyk: Inca officials recorded census figures, tribute and stored goods on khipus, knotted cords whose knot types and positions encoded numbers in a base-ten system.
ev: Pachacuti defeats the Chanka and launches Inca imperial expansion
Túpac Inca Yupanqui conquers the Kingdom of Chimor
Túpac Inca Yupanqui succeeds Pachacuti as Sapa Inca
Huayna Capac becomes Sapa Inca and extends the empire northwards
Huayna Capac dies of an epidemic, probably smallpox
Atahualpa defeats Huáscar, then is captured by Francisco Pizarro at Cajamarca
Atahualpa is executed and the Spaniards enter Cusco

f.successor: Neo-Inca State; Spanish Viceroyalty of Peru
